title: The San Jacinto headstone and the club's presidents
summary: Mitchell wishes he had saved the founders' headstone; he names presidents Warren Edwards and Monette, who lost the club's money, and Benzie (Edmund Fourier), who bought it.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You know what I had promised to do? I wanted to take that headstone from there, you know what I mean? It had all the names. You didn't get it? The founders and all, you know what I mean? Oh, you didn't get it? I couldn't get it, and people broke up.
Yeah, tore it up before you could get there. That would have been a wonderful thing to have.
You had all of the founders of the high car. Oh.
Yeah, do you know the oldest one that you could remember, the president of the club?
He was one of the presidents? Yeah.

Wow. And after him you had Monette. Yeah. That's the one that messed up all the money for the club, see what I mean? The club went down. Yeah. Then, uh, Benzie bought it out. His name is Edmund Fourier. Fourier, yeah.
Oh, I didn't know his name. His real name was Edmund? Yeah, Edmund Fourier.
I didn't know that. I just knew him about Benzie.
Yeah. I'll call him Papa Benzie. Yeah, yeah.
He bought the San Jacinto club?
